subject: Location boundary playbook and contract implications
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Li <daniel@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Location boundary playbook and contract implications

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Following up with a quick note so we have the scope captured in writing: HealthSync mentioned you need firm assurances that (a) primary inference and persistent artifacts for EU users remain within EU-resident infrastructure, and (b) short-lived cross-region processing is permitted for resilience/analytics with clearly bounded windows and audit traces.

To move this forward we need two things from your side:
- A data flow diagram (high level) that shows which workloads you consider EU data (user profiles, logs, embeddings, etc.).
- Any procurement/contract constraints (e.g., must be EU-only in the DPA, disallowed subprocessors, or special KMS requirements).

On our side I attached an early version of our internal location playbook (redwood_location_playbook_v0.9.pdf) so you can see how we categorize "anchored" vs "ephemeral" processing and the audit timeline we can provide. If you can share the data flow map today, I can loop in Legal and Solutions to propose precise DPA language.

Proposed next steps:
1) HealthSync sends data flow map and any procurement ask (attachment or link) — by EOD 12/08 if possible.
2) We draft a short DPA addendum with explicit "location boundaries" + temporary cross-region exceptions and a logging/notification SLA.
3) Quick review with your procurement/legal, then DocuSign.

Thanks — I copied Marissa so she can coordinate the operational mapping.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
Attachment: redwood_location_playbook_v0.9.pdf (pdf)

From: Daniel Li <daniel@healthsync.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 11:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Location boundary playbook and contract implications

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear summary and the playbook, that's helpful. I attached a simple dataflow spreadsheet so you can see which tables/events we consider EU-custody (HealthSync EU tenants). Quick answers to your bullets:

- Data flow map: attached (HealthSync_DataFlow_Map.xlsx). EU tenant PII + embeddings are marked as EU-resident.
- Procurement constraints: we need the DPA to state that processing and storage of EU tenant data will be anchored to EU regions by default. Temporary processing outside EU is allowed only for (i) emergency failover for 24 hours maximum, or (ii) scheduled analytics/ML re-training jobs that are notified 72h in advance.

Two additional asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a log of any short-lived cross-region processing within 12 hours of occurrence (CSV export or Drive link)?
2) We need a list of subprocessors with their locations and an expected date when each subprocessor became/will become active for HealthSync.

I'll be available on Thursday if you want to walk the flow together.

Cheers,
Daniel Li
Head of Infrastructure, HealthSync
daniel@healthsync.com
Attachment: HealthSync_DataFlow_Map.xlsx (xlsx)

Temporary processing outside EU is allowed only for (i) emergency failover for 24 hours maximum, or (ii) scheduled analytics/ML re-training jobs that are notified 72h in advance.
> 
> Two additional asks:
> 1) Can Redwood provide a log of any short-lived cross-region processing within 12 hours of occurrence (CSV export or Drive link)?
> 2) We need a list of subprocessors with their locations and an expected date when each subprocessor became/will become active for HealthSync.

Thanks, Daniel — I dropped this into our internal queue and copied Legal/Ops so we can turn around an initial DPA addendum and subprocessor roster.

Notes / responses to asks:
- Log of short-lived cross-region processing: Yes — Operational logs are available. For contract language we'll propose a 24-hour audit export with notification SLA of 12 hours (we can surface an export or share a Drive link).
- Subprocessors: I'll attach a draft roster. Kimberly, can you confirm the last activation dates for the listed subprocessors (GCS EU, KMS-EU-HSM, Metrics-Edge-EU)?

Jonas — can Legal prepare a DPA addendum draft that: (a) includes an EU anchoring guarantee for identified EU tenant data, (b) enumerates permitted cross-region windows (emergency 24h, scheduled jobs with 72h notice), and (c) defines the audit/export SLA (12h for listing and 24h for full export)?

If we can get a draft by EOD 12/10, I'll share with HealthSync procurement for a quick review.

Best,
Naomi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: DPA-addendum-draft.docx (placeholder to be filled by Legal)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Li <daniel@healthsync.com>, procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Location boundary playbook and contract implications

Thanks — I reviewed the flow and Naomi's summary. Quick legal position and proposed language for the addendum:

1) EU anchoring guarantee (proposed excerpt):

"Redwood Inference shall ensure that for the Customer's EU-tenants (as identified in HealthSync_DataFlow_Map.xlsx), primary processing and persistent storage of personal data shall be performed in EU-hosted infrastructure. Redwood may perform temporary cross-border processing only under the conditions described in Section 2 below. Documentation and audit logs will be made available per Section 4."

2) Permitted cross-region windows (proposed excerpt):

"Permitted cross-region processing is limited to: (a) emergency failover events not to exceed 24 continuous hours per event; and (b) scheduled analytics/ML jobs where Redwood provides at least 72 hours' prior notice to Customer. Redwood will record start/end timestamps and the affected datasets for each event."

3) Audit / export SLA (proposed excerpt):

"Within twelve (12) hours of Customer request, Redwood will provide a summary CSV identifying cross-region processing events (start timestamp, end timestamp, cause, and affected dataset). A full forensic export (where applicable) will be made available within twenty-four (24) hours subject to export format constraints and mutually agreed delivery mechanism."

4) Subprocessor roster: Kimberly — please attach the roster with activation dates and region locations. We'll include the roster as an annex (Annex A) to the addendum.

5) Next steps:
- Kimberly to attach roster by EOD 12/10.
- Legal to insert the above excerpts into DPA-addendum-draft.docx and share a Drive link + DocuSign wrapper for signature.
- Naomi to propose an ops runbook (handoff and notification flow) for scheduled analytics jobs.

I'll prepare the draft and upload to our shared drive (link below) and start a DocuSign envelope once Kimberly confirms the roster.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
